items.title: Google Explains Why 404 Errors Aren't Scary 👻
items.description: Google is out with a new video in The Non-Canonical Cabinet series, this one is on 404 pages and why they are not scary. I like how they also timed the video with a Halloween theme.

items.title: The Hreflang Magic Trick – It Routes, It Doesn’t Rank via @sejournal, @billhunt
items.description: Understand why Google can serve unindexed hreflang URLs and why market pages need unique local value to stand out in AI search. The post The Hreflang Magic Trick – It Routes, It Doesn’t Rank appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Decodo Launches Web Data API To Give AI Agents Web Access
items.description: Decodo has introduced Web Data API, combining scraping, searching, mapping, and crawling under one key for AI agents and retrieval pipelines. The post Decodo Launches Web Data API To Give AI Agents Web Access appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Google Search Fan POV (Point Of View) Button
items.description: Google has added a new interactive search button to some sports-related queries named "Fan POV." If you go to Google Search and search for [world series], Google will show a blue button that has a baseball emoji and the words "Fan POV." When you click on it, it opens a dialog box with drop downs that you can customize and then will take you into AI Mode to give you more information.

items.title: GA4 Missed 66% Of One Retailer’s Holiday Orders: Check Yours Before Peak Season
items.description: GA4 missed two-thirds of one retailer's holiday orders. What an audit of eight ecommerce brands found, and the check to run before peak season. The post GA4 Missed 66% Of One Retailer’s Holiday Orders: Check Yours Before Peak Season appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Google Ads Tests Sponsored Results With Apple Messages Button
items.description: Google is testing a new messaging button named Apple Messages on the Google Ads sponsored results. Google has placed messages button, message assets, on Google search ads for a long time now but I don't think I've seen the Apple Messages button before.

items.title: Google Ads "All Conversions" Tab Is Fully Live
items.description: Google Ads seems to have rolled out the "All conversions" tab within the Goals and Conversions section. This allows advertisers to make one less click, where they can avoid clicking on "View all conversion actions."

items.title: Google Business Profiles Adds Facebook Messenger M.me Links
items.description: Google is emailing businesses to let them know it is automatically adding Facebook (Meta) Messenger M.me links to their Google Business Profile. I don't think I've seen Google add m.me links to a Google Business Profile before, so this may be new.

items.title: Google Image Search Tests Save Button On Image Overlay
items.description: Google is testing a new position for the Save button within Google Image Search. When you hover your mouse cursor over an image, you may see a "Save" button show up that you can click on. The previous method was to show the Save button when you click on an image and the image preview shows up in a window.

items.title: Bing Tests Get Phone Number & QR Code To Scan
items.description: Microsoft Bing is testing adding a phone icon to the local pack on desktop, when you click on the phone button, it has a scan to call QR code with the phone number listed out. Google did this back in 2023 and now Microsoft Bing is testing it.

items.title: Google Business Profiles Asking Businesses For EIN
items.description: Google is asking some businesses to provide their EIN, Employer Identification Number and a link to their privacy policy when updating parts of their Google Business Profile.

items.title: Google Signals A Wider Crackdown On UGC SEO Spam via @sejournal, @martinibuster
items.description: Google signals that its fight against SEO spam is expanding to new kinds of platforms, tools, and services. The post Google Signals A Wider Crackdown On UGC SEO Spam appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Google: Disabled Discover Clicks Were A Bug In An Experiment via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.description: Rajan Patel wrote on X that disabled source clicks on Google Discover AI summaries were a bug in an experiment that has been turned off. The post Google: Disabled Discover Clicks Were A Bug In An Experiment appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Googlebot Must Follow Redirects From Homepage To Favicon, Updated Doc Say
items.description: Google Search has just updated its favicon documentation to now specify that Googlebot must be able to follow redirects from the homepage to the page where the favicon is specified. The document also explicitly says that these URLs must not be blocked by robots.txt or other means.

items.title: Why We Should Fear The Shadow Web We’re Building For AI via @sejournal, @chrisgreenseo
items.description: Why would an AI search provider keep trusting information a brand hides from its own website? The parallels with cloaking are too close to ignore. The post Why We Should Fear The Shadow Web We’re Building For AI appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Google Privacy Update Lets Connected Apps Shape AI Mode Ads via @sejournal, @brookeosmundson
items.description: Google is testing AI Mode ads informed by connected Gmail and Photos data, as its privacy policy adds an exception for ad personalization. The post Google Privacy Update Lets Connected Apps Shape AI Mode Ads appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Shopify Retires Knowledge Base App, Moves AI Agent Facts To Admin via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.description: Shopify's AI agent knowledge base now lives in the admin. Policies and contact details publish by default. Some app users need to re-add their facts. The post Shopify Retires Knowledge Base App, Moves AI Agent Facts To Admin appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: ChatGPT Data: 1 In 5 Consumer Messages Now Seek Information via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.description: Looking things up now makes up about as large a share of consumer ChatGPT messages as writing, though the increase is smaller than earlier data. The post ChatGPT Data: 1 In 5 Consumer Messages Now Seek Information appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: How I Decide Where The Next $100,000 Of Marketing Budget Should Go
items.description: Allocate your next marketing budget increase by weighing retention and conversion fixes against more paid search, then fund the bottleneck with evidence. The post How I Decide Where The Next $100,000 Of Marketing Budget Should Go appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.description: Jonathan Berthold explains why bottom-of-funnel content is the lowest-lift experiment and how to sell leadership on a test you can't promise will win. The post Flat Traffic, No Budget: What Ziff Davis’ Jonathan Berthold Tests First appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Unconfirmed Google Search Ranking Update: Volatility & Chatter Spike
items.description: I know I just reported on an unconfirmed Google Search ranking update from this past Saturday, October 24th. But I am now seeing a larger spike in volatility, along with an increase in SEO community chatter around another unconfirmed update over the past 24 hours.

items.title: Google Downplays The Importance Of Fresh Index Reporting
items.description: Google's John Mueller kind of downplayed the importance of the freshness of the Google Search Console page indexing report. He said on Reddit, in response to my coverage of the report's recent slowness, that "it can feel like it's important to focus on it, but honestly, save your energy."

items.title: Advertisers Can't Figure Out If An Ad Is A Google Local Service Ad Or Not
items.description: Google advertisers are struggling to agree on whether a specific local ad unit in Google Search is a Local Service Ad or another type of local Google ad.

items.title: Google Ads Tests Dotted Underlined Links In Sponsored Results
items.description: Google is testing placing dotted underlined links in the sponsored results ad descriptions. When you click on them, you go to the ad destination's URL, like you would if you clicked on the title of the ad.

items.title: Google Responds To Concern Over Search Console Indexing Reports via @sejournal, @martinibuster
items.description: John Mueller's responded to a stalled indexing report and explained why SEOs may need to relax about indexing report freshness. The post Google Responds To Concern Over Search Console Indexing Reports appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Google Ads Expands Customer Lifecycle Goals In Search And Shopping via @sejournal, @brookeosmundson
items.description: Google Ads expands customer lifecycle goals with High Value acquisition for Shopping and retention modes across Search, Shopping, and Performance Max. The post Google Ads Expands Customer Lifecycle Goals In Search And Shopping appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Google Updates Spam Guide For Shared Pages, Generated Content & Apps via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.description: New spam guidance says to noindex or block crawling on pages made for sharing. Google's docs say a URL blocked in robots.txt can be indexed. The post Google Updates Spam Guide For Shared Pages, Generated Content & Apps appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Generative UI Could Turn Google Into Your Booking.com via @sejournal, @slobodanmanic
items.description: Wait for Google to send the booking, or build channels you own. That choice does not need to wait for generative UI. The post Generative UI Could Turn Google Into Your Booking.com appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Your Google Ads Account Is Hitting Its Targets, So Why Isn’t The Business Growing?
items.description: Spot the gaps between Google Ads targets and business growth, from outdated margins and repeat buyers to weak leads and capped reach. The post Your Google Ads Account Is Hitting Its Targets, So Why Isn’t The Business Growing? appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Google Gets The Thank-You via @sejournal, @pedrodias
items.description: Referral reports show who sent the visit, not who shaped the decision. Why GEO’s real job is what a model learns, not what it retrieves. The post Google Gets The Thank-You appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: Meta Pushes Its Updated Business Terms Back To Nov. 20 via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.description: Meta delayed its updated business terms amid complaints to EU and UK regulators. The permission to crawl sites tied to its business users hasn't changed. The post Meta Pushes Its Updated Business Terms Back To Nov. 20 appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: ChatGPT Rarely Named Some Brands Even When Sources Mentioned Them via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
items.description: Brands logged-out ChatGPT rarely named without search also showed up less when it searched, even with cited-page coverage, in new comparison-prompt data. The post ChatGPT Rarely Named Some Brands Even When Sources Mentioned Them appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.description: Reddit's community-first plans strengthen the case for brand subreddits built around useful answers and relationships that bring people back. The post At Mod World, Reddit’s CEO Just Gave Brands More Reasons To Build Their Own Communities appeared first on Search Engine Journal .

items.title: New learning paths: curated YouTube playlists for Search fundamentals and Technical SEO
items.description: Over the years, the Search Central YouTube channel has published hundreds of videos across various series, from Search for Beginners and Ask Googlebot to Search Console Training and Search Off the Record. While our series structure works well for deep dives and episodic updates, we know that finding a clear, sequential learning path from scratch can sometimes be challenging.

items.title: Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console
items.description: Understanding how users find your content is crucial for any publisher or site owner. As Search evolves to include more visual and multimodal experiences, we want to ensure you have the data you need to analyze your performance.

items.title: Search Central Live Deep Dive Europe 2026: Meet the community speakers
items.description: It's happening! We are absolutely pumped that we're just about two weeks away from Search Central Live Deep Dive Europe 2026! From September 30 to October 2, 2026, the Google Search Central team is heading to the gorgeous city of Barcelona, Spain for three days of deep technical exploration, networking, and collaboration.

items.title: Search Central Live India 2026: Bengaluru, We're Coming (For Real This Time)
items.description: Remember back in March when we told our Indian community to "sit tight" while we figured out the APAC event calendar? Hopefully, you didn't take that too literally, because sitting tight for six months is probably not great for your back. In any case, you can finally stand up and stretch: Search Central Live is officially returning to India in 2026, specifically to Bengaluru!

items.description: Leer en español

items.title: Update to the Site Reputation Policy
items.description: In 2024, we introduced our site reputation policy to stop a practice where third-party content is published on a trusted website just to exploit that site's good reputation to rank higher in Search. This practice hurts search quality, and creates a bad experience for users.

items.title: Platform properties roll out globally, plus a new social and video performance guide
items.description: Earlier this month, we announced platform properties for Search Console, allowing you to track how your social and video posts on Instagram, TikTok, X, and YouTube perform on Google Search, Discover, and Google News. Today, platform properties are globally available to everyone.

items.title: See how content from social and video platforms performs on Google Search
items.description: Content creators and publishers use many channels beyond their own websites to reach their audiences. As people gravitate toward firsthand perspectives and different content formats, we want to make it easier for site owners and creators&mdash;even those without their own website&mdash;to get a consolidated view of how all of their content is getting discovered on Search.

items.title: Search Central Deep Dive Europe 2026: Apparently we're going to Barcelona
items.description: We're excited to officially announce the next stop for Search Central Live Deep Dive Europe 2026! Mark your calendars: based directly on your feedback, we're headed to Barcelona, Spain, from September 30 to October 2, 2026.

items.title: Help Us Pick the Next Stop in Europe for Search Central Live Deep Dive 2026!
items.description: As we mentioned a few months ago, we are bringing the Search Central Live Deep Dive format to the EMEA region. This SCL format requires finding the absolute best home for the event&mdash;a place where all of you can truly connect, learn, and enjoy.
